lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: FIFA has just confirmed that the UK will host the 2035 Women's World Cup.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Which is a big moment for a country that once kept women off its football grounds. For fifty years.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 1917, women at a munitions factory in Preston started playing football on their lunch breaks. Then they beat the factory's men.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: By Boxing Day 1920, the Dick, Kerr Ladies were drawing fifty-three thousand people to Goodison Park.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: A year later, the FA declared football quite unsuitable for females, and told its clubs not to let women use their grounds.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: So they were banned for selling too many tickets.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: FIFA's first Women's World Cup came in 1991, with eighty-minute matches, and officially it wasn't even called a World Cup. It was the First FIFA World Championship for Women's Football for the M and M's Cup.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 2023, almost two million people went to the World Cup. England are now two-time European champions.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And 2035 will have forty-eight teams, a hundred and four matches, and around four and a half million tickets.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Most of the players who'll star in it are kids right now, in a park somewhere.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 1921, women's football should not be encouraged. In 2035, the whole world is coming to watch it. The full story is on our channel.
